taskTitle: Where ten HTTP header fields are defined

checks.detail: 3 proposers ran in parallel, one per lens
4 phases had the tools designed for them

finalText:
RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics) and RFC 9111 (HTTP Caching) are the current definitions for the core HTTP fields. RFC 9111's header says "Obsoletes: 7234". RFC 9110 obsoletes RFC 7231 and RFC 7232, and its §1.4 lists the specifications it obsoletes. Strict-Transport-Security stays in RFC 6797 and Link stays in RFC 8288. Neither page carries an "Obsoleted by" notice, and RFC 8288's header says "Obsoletes: 5988". The RFC Editor info pages could not be opened, so the status of those two is based on that absence and on a search that found no replacement. That is not conclusive.

- Age: RFC 9111 §5.1, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111.html
- Cache-Control: RFC 9111 §5.2, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111.html
- Expires: RFC 9111 §5.3, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111.html
- Last-Modified: RFC 9110 §8.8.2, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html
- ETag: RFC 9110 §8.8.3, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html
- Location: RFC 9110 §10.2.2, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html
- Retry-After: RFC 9110 §10.2.3, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html
- Vary: RFC 9110 §12.5.5, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html
- Strict-Transport-Security: RFC 6797 §6.1, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6797.html
- Link: RFC 8288 §3, https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8288.html

The Age sentence wraps across lines in the page text, so it is joined with single spaces below.
